problem: Embodied AI agents feed general-purpose visual features (e.g., CLIP) into a small recurrent policy. These features carry much task-irrelevant information (textures, colors, distractor objects), and the few policy parameters must both filter it and decide actions. This hurts convergence and generalization.
motivation: Human selective attention (inattentional blindness, top-down search) filters perception by task goals. Applying this to agents should decouple 'what to perceive' from 'how to act', giving faster training, better transfer to new visual domains and more efficient behavior.
key_idea: Insert a small task-conditioned learnable codebook bottleneck (256 codes x 10 dims, softmax attention with dropout) between the goal-fused visual embedding and the recurrent policy, trained end-to-end with the RL reward only.
insight: Goal-conditioning is essential: putting the codebook before goal fusion drops ProcTHOR SR from 73.4 to 65.3, and the baseline is 59.81. Dropout on the code probabilities prevents imbalanced code usage (SR 62.5 to 71.4 on ProcTHOR at 150M steps). Because the codebook separates perception from decision-making, freezing the policy and finetuning only the adaptation module transfers much better to Habitat (SR 36.45 to 50.25). Probing shows the bottleneck keeps goal visibility and distance information but loses general object presence.
method: Codebook module: K=256 learnable codes of dimension D_c=10, randomly initialized, placed after the goal/action/vision fusion (E in R^1568) and before the RNN.

Scoring function: a single-layer MLP followed by softmax gives a probability simplex over the codes. The compact h is the convex combination of the codes, and a linear layer upsamples h to E_hat, which feeds the recurrent state encoder and actor-critic.
Dropout regularization: dropout of 0.1 on the code probabilities prevents codebook collapse; it worked better than Linde-Buzo-Gray splitting and Gumbel softmax.

Training: PPO (DD-PPO for the displacement task) jointly optimizes the codebook, encoders and policy on the task reward only. Pretrained on ProcTHOR-10k for 435M steps and evaluated zero-shot elsewhere.

Lightweight adaptation to Habitat: only the CNN layers after the frozen CLIP, the goal/action embedders and the codebook scoring function are finetuned; the codebook, RNN and actor-critic stay frozen.
New metric SEL (Success weighted by Episode Length) plus trajectory curvature, to capture step efficiency and smoothness that SPL misses.
Backbone variants: the codebook is also applied on top of DINOv2 ViT-S/14 and to m-VOLE for object displacement.

setting.backbone: EmbCLIP (frozen CLIP ResNet-50 + small CNN + 1-layer GRU 512 + actor-critic) with codebook, trained with PPO; m-VOLE for manipulation
setting.model_size: codebook is tiny (256x10 codes); CLIP RN50 frozen; RNN 512 hidden units
setting.training_data: RL on ProcTHOR-10k houses for 435M steps (ObjectNav); APND dataset with 20 train kitchen scenes for 20M steps (displacement); Habitat finetuning for 200M steps starting from the 200M-step checkpoint
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (plus depth, segmentation mask and end-effector sensor for displacement), goal object category
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MoveAhead, RotateRight/Left, LookUp/Down, Done (arm-move actions for manipulation)
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR family (ProcTHOR, ArchitecTHOR, RoboTHOR, AI2-iTHOR, ManipulaTHOR); Habitat (HM3D) for transfer
setting.privileged: none at test time (an expert with privileged simulator info is used only to compute the SEL metric; GT segmentation masks are used for m-VOLE per its setup)

results: The codebook improves SR on all four ObjectNav benchmarks over EmbCLIP (e.g., ProcTHOR 67.70→73.72, AI2-iTHOR 70.00→78.40) and lowers episode length and curvature, while SPL is slightly lower. It also improves m-VOLE on displacement (SR 59.6→65.1). With lightweight Habitat finetuning it reaches SR 50.25 vs 36.45 for EmbCLIP.
limitations: SPL is slightly lower than the baseline on several benchmarks, and performance remains bounded by the frozen encoder's perception (small objects are missed) and by incomplete exploration.
Full end-to-end finetuning in Habitat gives no gain over the baseline (SR 55.0 vs 58.0).
Evaluated only in simulation on ObjectNav and object displacement, with no real-robot experiments; some ablations use different step budgets.
